claim: Metastasis is a major cause of cancer mortality.
source: Metastasis is a major cause of cancer mortality.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about cancer mortality.

claim: A transgenic mouse model was generated whereby conditional expression of MYC and Twist1 enables hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) to metastasize in >90% of mice.
source: We generated an autochthonous transgenic mouse model whereby conditional expression of MYC and Twist1 enables hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) to metastasize in >90% of mice.
evidence: The manuscript describes the generation of a mouse model and reports the metastasis rate observed in experiments.

claim: MYC and Twist1 cooperate to elicit a transcriptional program associated with the activation of innate immunity.
source: MYC and Twist1 cooperate and their sustained expression is required to elicit a transcriptional program associated with the activation of innate immunity, through secretion of a cytokinome that elicits recruitment and polarization of tumor associated macrophages (TAMs).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing transcriptional changes and immune cell recruitment in the mouse model.

claim: MYC and Twist1 induce secretion of a cytokinome that elicits recruitment and polarization of tumor associated macrophages (TAMs).
source: MYC and Twist1 cooperate and their sustained expression is required to elicit a transcriptional program associated with the activation of innate immunity, through secretion of a cytokinome that elicits recruitment and polarization of tumor associated macrophages (TAMs).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing cytokine secretion and macrophage recruitment/polarization.

claim: Systemic treatment with Ccl2 and Il13 induced MYC-HCCs to metastasize.
source: Systemic treatment with Ccl2 and Il13 induced MYC-HCCs to metastasize; whereas, blockade of Ccl2 and Il13 abrogated MYC/Twist1-HCC metastasis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from in vivo treatment studies.

claim: Blockade of Ccl2 and Il13 abrogated MYC/Twist1-HCC metastasis.
source: Systemic treatment with Ccl2 and Il13 induced MYC-HCCs to metastasize; whereas, blockade of Ccl2 and Il13 abrogated MYC/Twist1-HCC metastasis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from antibody blockade studies.

claim: In 33 human cancers (n = 9502) MYC and TWIST1 predict poor survival (p=4.3×10−10).
source: Further, in 33 human cancers (n = 9502) MYC and TWIST1 predict poor survival (p=4.3×10−10), CCL2/IL13 expression (p<10−109) and TAM infiltration (p<10−96).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of TCGA data.

claim: In 33 human cancers (n = 9502) MYC and TWIST1 predict CCL2/IL13 expression (p<10−109).
source: Further, in 33 human cancers (n = 9502) MYC and TWIST1 predict poor survival (p=4.3×10−10), CCL2/IL13 expression (p<10−109) and TAM infiltration (p<10−96).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis of TCGA data.

claim: In 33 human cancers (n = 9502) MYC and TWIST1 predict TAM infiltration (p<10−96).
source: Further, in 33 human cancers (n = 9502) MYC and TWIST1 predict poor survival (p=4.3×10−10), CCL2/IL13 expression (p<10−109) and TAM infiltration (p<10−96).
evidence: This is supported by CIBERSORT analysis of TCGA data.

claim: In the plasma of patients with HCC (n = 25) but not cirrhosis (n = 10), CCL2 and IL13 were increased.
source: Finally, in the plasma of patients with HCC (n = 25) but not cirrhosis (n = 10), CCL2 and IL13 were increased and IL13 predicted invasive tumors.
evidence: This is supported by clinical data from patient plasma samples.

claim: IL13 predicted invasive tumors in patients with HCC.
source: Finally, in the plasma of patients with HCC (n = 25) but not cirrhosis (n = 10), CCL2 and IL13 were increased and IL13 predicted invasive tumors.
evidence: This is supported by clinical correlation analysis.

claim: MYC and TWIST1 generally cooperate in human cancer to elicit a cytokinome that enables metastasis through crosstalk between cancer and immune microenvironment.
source: Therefore, MYC and TWIST1 generally appear to cooperate in human cancer to elicit a cytokinome that enables metastasis through crosstalk between cancer and immune microenvironment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of experimental and clinical data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Metastasis occurs when tumor cells gain the ability to invade, migrate and colonize distant sites.
source: Metastasis occur when tumor cells gain the ability to invade, migrate and colonize distant sites, and this accounts for most of the morbidity and mortality associated with cancer (Mehlen and Puisieux, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Metastasis accounts for most of the morbidity and mortality associated with cancer.
source: Metastasis occur when tumor cells gain the ability to invade, migrate and colonize distant sites, and this accounts for most of the morbidity and mortality associated with cancer (Mehlen and Puisieux, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Innate immune cells, especially tumor associated macrophages (TAMs), contribute to metastasis through multiple mechanisms.
source: Innate immune cells, especially tumor associated macrophages (TAMs), are known to contribute to metastasis through multiple mechanisms including effects on angiogenesis, production of specific cytokines, suppression of the immune system, and induction of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) (Gonzalez et al., 2018; Lu et al., 2011; Qian and Pollard, 2010; Wan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: TAMs contribute to metastasis through effects on angiogenesis, production of specific cytokines, suppression of the immune system, and induction of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT).
source: Innate immune cells, especially tumor associated macrophages (TAMs), are known to contribute to metastasis through multiple mechanisms including effects on angiogenesis, production of specific cytokines, suppression of the immune system, and induction of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) (Gonzalez et al., 2018; Lu et al., 2011; Qian and Pollard, 2010; Wan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The MYC oncogene is a transcription factor that is one of the most commonly activated oncogenes in the pathogenesis of many types of human cancer including HCC.
source: The MYC oncogene is a transcription factor that is one of the most commonly activated oncogenes in the pathogenesis of many types of human cancer including HCC (Schaub et al., 2018; Dang, 2012; Gabay et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Murine MYC-driven HCC do not metastasize.
source: But murine MYC-driven HCC do not metastasize.
evidence: This is an observation from the authors' mouse model.

claim: Twist1 is a transcription factor that is important during embryogenesis for normal cellular migration.
source: Twist1 is a transcription factor that is important during embryogenesis for normal cellular migration (Lee et al., 1999; Thisse et al., 1987).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Twist1 has been shown to be an important gene product that can enable mouse and human tumor cell lines to acquire the ability to metastasize associated with EMT.
source: Twist1 has been shown to be an important gene product that can enable mouse and human tumor cell lines to acquire the ability to metastasize associated with EMT (Thiery et al., 2009; Xu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Co-expression of MYC and Twist1 leads to widely metastatic and invasive HCC.
source: Here we used the Tet System to conditionally express Twist1 in combination with MYC to show that their co-expression leads to widely metastatic and invasive HCC.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the mouse model.

claim: Cancer cell-intrinsic properties like proliferation, apoptosis or invasiveness were not different between the non-metastatic MYC-HCC and the metastatic MYC/Twist1-HCC.
source: Cancer cell-intrinsic properties like proliferation, apoptosis or invasiveness were not different between the non-metastatic MYC-HCC and the metastatic MYC/Twist1-HCC.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing the two tumor types.

claim: Metastatic progression was dependent on the ability of MYC and Twist1 to dramatically reprogram the tumor innate immune microenvironment.
source: Instead, metastatic progression was dependent on the ability of MYC and Twist1 to dramatically reprogram the tumor innate immune microenvironment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data showing immune microenvironment changes.

claim: MYC and Twist1 induce the cancer cell to secrete cytokines like Ccl2 and Il13 that lead to recruitment and polarization of macrophages respectively.
source: Together, MYC and Twist1 induce the cancer cell to secrete cytokines like Ccl2 and Il13 that lead to recruitment and polarization of macrophages respectively, thus causing metastasis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from in vitro and in vivo studies.

claim: Systemically administering Ccl2 and Il13 is sufficient to cause metastasis of MYC-HCC.
source: Systemically, administering Ccl2 and Il13 is sufficient to cause metastasis of MYC-HCC and, conversely blocking these specific cytokines profoundly inhibits metastasis in MYC/Twist1 HCC.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from in vivo treatment studies.

claim: Blocking Ccl2 and Il13 profoundly inhibits metastasis in MYC/Twist1 HCC.
source: Systemically, administering Ccl2 and Il13 is sufficient to cause metastasis of MYC-HCC and, conversely blocking these specific cytokines profoundly inhibits metastasis in MYC/Twist1 HCC.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from antibody blockade studies.

claim: Twist1 transgenic mice (LAP-tTA/TRE-Twist1/Luc) exhibited no disease nor gross or microscopic pathology for as long as 18 months of observation.
source: Twist1 transgenic mice (LAP-tTA/TRE-Twist1/Luc) exhibited no disease nor gross or microscopic pathology for as long as 18 months of observation thus demonstrating that Twist1 did not play a role in autochthonous tumorigenesis when overexpressed in the liver (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by observational data from the mouse model and referenced figure.

claim: Twist1 did not play a role in autochthonous tumorigenesis when overexpressed in the liver.
source: Twist1 transgenic mice (LAP-tTA/TRE-Twist1/Luc) exhibited no disease nor gross or microscopic pathology for as long as 18 months of observation thus demonstrating that Twist1 did not play a role in autochthonous tumorigenesis when overexpressed in the liver (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from observational data.

claim: Both MYC and MYC/Twist1 mice develop multifocal liver cancer.
source: Both MYC and MYC/Twist1 mice were observed to develop multifocal liver cancer, while only MYC/Twist1 mice developed lung metastases (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data from the mouse model.

claim: Only MYC/Twist1 mice developed lung metastases.
source: Both MYC and MYC/Twist1 mice were observed to develop multifocal liver cancer, while only MYC/Twist1 mice developed lung metastases (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data from the mouse model.

claim: MYC/Twist1 mice were moribund with HCC sooner and had a median survival of 25 months compared to 32 months in MYC mice (p<0.001).
source: MYC/Twist1 mice were moribund with HCC sooner and had a median survival of 25 months compared to 32 months in MYC mice (p<0.001, Figure 1e).
evidence: This is supported by survival data from the mouse model.

claim: MYC mice rarely exhibited metastasis even after extended observation (2%, n = 50).
source: MYC mice rarely exhibited metastasis even after extended observation (2%, n = 50, Figure 1f); whereas, MYC/Twist1 mice regularly exhibited rapid onset of metastasis with high penetrance (90%) -metastases to the lungs (70%), peritoneum (60%) and lymph nodes (20%) (n = 50, Figure 1f).
evidence: This is supported by observational data from the mouse model.

claim: MYC/Twist1 mice regularly exhibited rapid onset of metastasis with high penetrance (90%).
source: MYC mice rarely exhibited metastasis even after extended observation (2%, n = 50, Figure 1f); whereas, MYC/Twist1 mice regularly exhibited rapid onset of metastasis with high penetrance (90%) -metastases to the lungs (70%), peritoneum (60%) and lymph nodes (20%) (n = 50, Figure 1f).
evidence: This is supported by observational data from the mouse model.

claim: MYC/Twist1 mice exhibited metastases to the lungs (70%), peritoneum (60%) and lymph nodes (20%).
source: MYC mice rarely exhibited metastasis even after extended observation (2%, n = 50, Figure 1f); whereas, MYC/Twist1 mice regularly exhibited rapid onset of metastasis with high penetrance (90%) -metastases to the lungs (70%), peritoneum (60%) and lymph nodes (20%) (n = 50, Figure 1f).
evidence: This is supported by observational data from the mouse model.

claim: Twist1 combined with MYC expression in liver cells elicits HCC metastasis.
source: Thus, Twist1 combined with MYC expression in liver cells elicits HCC metastasis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The tumor burden in the liver was not statistically different between MYC and MYC/Twist1 mice.
source: Against this possibility, the tumor burden in the liver was not statistically different between MYC and MYC/Twist1 mice (Figure 1g).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data from the mouse model.

claim: There was no difference in the gross or microscopic appearance of MYC- and MYC/Twist1-HCC.
source: Also, there was no difference in the gross or microscopic appearance of MYC- and MYC/Twist1-HCC (Figure 1h–i).
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis.

claim: MYC levels were similar between MYC and MYC/Twist1 tumor models.
source: We considered that Twist1 could be influencing MYC expression levels, but MYC levels were similar between the two tumor models, while Twist1 was only overexpressed in the MYC/Twist1-HCC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c-d).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR and immunoblotting data.

claim: Twist1 was only overexpressed in the MYC/Twist1-HCC.
source: We considered that Twist1 could be influencing MYC expression levels, but MYC levels were similar between the two tumor models, while Twist1 was only overexpressed in the MYC/Twist1-HCC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c-d).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR and immunoblotting data.

claim: Tumor cell proliferative index and apoptosis between MYC- and MYC/Twist1-HCC were not different.
source: Tumor cell proliferative index (phospho histone three expression) and apoptosis (cleaved caspase three) between MYC- and MYC/Twist1-HCC were not different (Figure 1j–1k).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data.

claim: Primary tumor-derived cell lines from MYC- and MYC/Twist1-HCC did not show any difference in migratory capacity.
source: Primary tumor-derived cell lines from MYC- and MYC/Twist1-HCC did not show any difference in migratory capacity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: This is supported by wound healing assay data.

claim: There were no significant differences in the expression of multiple epithelial and mesenchymal markers between MYC and MYC/Twist1 tumors.
source: Lastly, Twist1 is a regulator of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) 26,37, but we did not observe significant differences in the expression of multiple epithelial and mesenchymal markers between MYC and MYC/Twist1 tumors (Figure 1—figure supplement 1f).
evidence: This is supported by transcriptomic data.

claim: Twist1 drives metastasis of MYC-induced HCC without affecting primary tumor burden, MYC expression, tumor cell proliferation, apoptosis, invasiveness or EMT markers.
source: Therefore, Twist1 drives metastasis of MYC-induced HCC without affecting primary tumor burden, MYC expression, tumor cell proliferation, apoptosis, invasiveness or EMT markers.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental observations.

claim: MYC- and MYC/Twist1-HCC have overall distinct, non-overlapping expression profiles that clustered separately.
source: Through unsupervised hierarchical clustering using principal component analysis (PCA), MYC- and MYC/Twist1-HCC were found to have overall distinct, non-overlapping expression profiles that clustered separately (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by RNA sequencing and PCA analysis.

claim: 514 genes (220 up and 294 down) were differentially expressed between MYC-HCC and MYC/Twist1-HCC (p<0.001, q < 0.05, fold change ≥2).
source: A comparative analysis identified 514 genes (220 up and 294 down) that were differentially expressed between MYC-HCC and MYC/Twist1-HCC (p<0.001, q < 0.05, fold change ≥2) (Figure 2b, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by RNA sequencing data analysis.

claim: The top biological processes upregulated in MYC/Twist1-HCC involved inflammatory responses including leukocyte infiltration, myeloid cell and granulocyte recruitment.
source: Functional pathway analysis revealed the top biological processes upregulated in MYC/Twist1-HCC involved inflammatory responses including leukocyte infiltration, myeloid cell and granulocyte recruitment (Figure 2b, Figure 2—figure supplement 1a, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by pathway analysis of RNA sequencing data.

claim: M2 macrophages were significantly enriched in MYC/Twist1 tumors according to CIBERSORT analysis.
source: CIBERSORT (Newman et al., 2015) identified M2 macrophages to be significantly enriched in MYC/Twist1 tumors, of the 22 immune subsets analyzed (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is supported by CIBERSORT analysis of RNA sequencing data, with citation to the method.

claim: MYC/Twist1-HCC exhibited a 15-fold shift in the ratio of M2 to M1 macrophages when compared to MYC tumors.
source: MYC/Twist1-HCC exhibited a 15-fold shift in the ratio of M2 to M1 macrophages when compared to MYC tumors (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is supported by CIBERSORT analysis data.

claim: No significant differences in other major immune compartments were seen including B cells, T cells, NK cells, dendritic cells, neutrophils, or mast cells.
source: No significant differences in other major immune compartments were seen including- B cells, T cells, NK cells, dendritic cells, neutrophils, or mast cells (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is supported by CIBERSORT analysis data.

claim: Increased macrophage infiltration was confirmed in MYC/Twist1 primary and metastatic tumors by IHC.
source: Increased macrophage infiltration in MYC/Twist1 primary and metastatic tumors (Figure 2e) with no change in neutrophils or CD4 T cells infiltration was confirmed by IHC (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data.

claim: There was no change in neutrophils or CD4 T cells infiltration between MYC and MYC/Twist1 tumors.
source: Increased macrophage infiltration in MYC/Twist1 primary and metastatic tumors (Figure 2e) with no change in neutrophils or CD4 T cells infiltration was confirmed by IHC (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data.

claim: TAMs isolated from primary MYC/Twist1-HCC had increased macrophages of the M2 phenotype (Cd206High/Arg1High), more specifically a M2a phenotype.
source: TAMs isolated from primary MYC/Twist1-HCC had increased macrophages of the M2 phenotype (Cd206High/Arg1High), more specifically a M2a phenotype (Figure 2f).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR analysis of isolated macrophages.

claim: Induction of MYC and Twist1 expression is associated with tumor initiation and rapid onset of macrophage infiltration in early tumors which increases during tumor progression.
source: Induction of MYC and Twist1 expression is associated with tumor initiation and rapid onset of macrophage infiltration in early tumors which increases during tumor progression.
evidence: This is supported by temporal analysis of macrophage infiltration.

claim: The inactivation of MYC and Twist1 in tumors shows rapid and complete tumor regression in all observed mice (n = 20) within 2 weeks.
source: Conversely, the inactivation of MYC and Twist1 in tumors shows rapid and complete tumor regression in all observed mice (n = 20) within 2 weeks (Figure 2—figure supplement 1c) and also prompt exodus of macrophages (Figure 2g–2h).
evidence: This is supported by imaging and histological data from oncogene inactivation experiments.

claim: The inactivation of MYC and Twist1 in tumors results in prompt exodus of macrophages.
source: Conversely, the inactivation of MYC and Twist1 in tumors shows rapid and complete tumor regression in all observed mice (n = 20) within 2 weeks (Figure 2—figure supplement 1c) and also prompt exodus of macrophages (Figure 2g–2h).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data.

claim: Conditioned media from TAMs isolated from MYC/Twist1-HCC but not MYC-HCC increased the invasiveness of both MYC- and MYC/Twist1-HCC tumor cells in vitro.
source: Conditioned media from TAMs isolated from MYC/Twist1-HCC but not MYC-HCC increased the invasiveness of both MYC- and MYC/Twist1-HCC tumor cells in vitro (Figure 3a–3c).
evidence: This is supported by wound healing assay data.

claim: The inactivation of either MYC or Twist1 abrogated the ability of the cells to develop lung metastasis when injected intravenously in NSG mice.
source: We observed that the inactivation of either MYC or Twist1 abrogated the ability of the cells to develop lung metastasis when injected intravenously in NOD scid gamma (NSG) mice, while cells expressing both MYC and Twist1 led to development of extensive lung metastasis with prominent macrophage infiltration (Figure 3e–3f, Figure 3—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: Cells expressing both MYC and Twist1 led to development of extensive lung metastasis with prominent macrophage infiltration when injected intravenously in NSG mice.
source: We observed that the inactivation of either MYC or Twist1 abrogated the ability of the cells to develop lung metastasis when injected intravenously in NOD scid gamma (NSG) mice, while cells expressing both MYC and Twist1 led to development of extensive lung metastasis with prominent macrophage infiltration (Figure 3e–3f, Figure 3—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: MYC and Twist1 cooperate, and are both required to induce metastasis of HCC by a macrophage dependent mechanism.
source: Thus, MYC and Twist1 cooperate, and are both required to induce metastasis of HCC by a macrophage dependent mechanism.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental observations.

claim: Orthotopic implantation of MYC/Twist1- but not MYC-HCC tumor cells in NSG mice led to pulmonary and intrahepatic metastases with extensive macrophage infiltration.
source: Orthotopic implantation (Figure 4a) of MYC/Twist1- but not MYC-HCC tumor cells in NSG mice led to pulmonary and intrahepatic metastases with extensive macrophage infiltration (Figure 4b–c, Figure 4—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: Macrophage depletion with clodronate liposomes in mice orthotopically transplanted with MYC/Twist1-HCC had reduced intrahepatic (p=0.0006, FC 4.4) and lung metastases (p<0.0001, FC 8.8).
source: Macrophage depletion with clodronate liposomes (Moreno, 2018) but not control liposomes, in mice orthotopically transplanted with MYC/Twist1-HCC had reduced intrahepatic (p=0.0006, FC 4.4) and lung metastases (p<0.0001, FC 8.8) (Figure 4e–f).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data with clodronate treatment, with citation to the method.

claim: Clodronate was confirmed to remove macrophages but not affect tumor cells.
source: Note, clodronate was confirmed to remove macrophages but not affect tumor cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c-d).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro experimental data.

claim: Intravenous injection of MYC/Twist1-HCC but not MYC-HCC cells resulted in pulmonary metastases associated with macrophage infiltration.
source: Intravenous injection of MYC/Twist1-HCC but not MYC-HCC cells resulted in pulmonary metastases associated with macrophage infiltration (Figure 4g–i, Figure 4—figure supplement 1g).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: Clodronate depletion of macrophages almost completely abrogated pulmonary metastasis (p=0.0003, FC 4.3) in the lung trap assay.
source: Clodronate depletion of macrophages, almost completely abrogated pulmonary metastasis (p=0.0003, FC 4.3) (Figure 4j–4l).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: Twist1 elicits metastasis of MYC-HCC and promotes the invasiveness and colonization of metastases by a macrophage-dependent mechanism.
source: Therefore, Twist1 elicits metastasis of MYC-HCC and promotes the invasiveness and colonization of metastases by a macrophage-dependent mechanism.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental observations.

claim: Conditioned media derived from MYC/Twist1- but not MYC-HCC cells was sufficient to promote the migration of macrophages towards cancer cells.
source: Conditioned media derived from MYC/Twist1- but not MYC-HCC cells (Figure 5a) was sufficient to promote the migration of macrophages towards cancer cells (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is supported by transwell migration assay data.

claim: Conditioned media from MYC/Twist1- but not MYC-HCC cells was able to elicit changes in the morphology of macrophages to resemble M2 phenotype.
source: Conditioned media from MYC/Twist1- but not MYC-HCC cells was able to elicit changes in the morphology of macrophages to resemble M2 phenotype (McWhorter et al., 2013) (Figure 5c) and increased expression of M2 markers: Cd206, Arg1 and Cc3cr1 (Figure 5c), but not M1 markers: iNos, Ccr2, Ifnar2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by morphological analysis and qPCR data, with citation to the morphology reference.

claim: Conditioned media from MYC/Twist1- but not MYC-HCC cells increased expression of M2 markers: Cd206, Arg1 and Cc3cr1.
source: Conditioned media from MYC/Twist1- but not MYC-HCC cells was able to elicit changes in the morphology of macrophages to resemble M2 phenotype (McWhorter et al., 2013) (Figure 5c) and increased expression of M2 markers: Cd206, Arg1 and Cc3cr1 (Figure 5c), but not M1 markers: iNos, Ccr2, Ifnar2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data.

claim: Conditioned media from MYC/Twist1-HCC cells did not increase M1 markers: iNos, Ccr2, Ifnar2.
source: Conditioned media from MYC/Twist1- but not MYC-HCC cells was able to elicit changes in the morphology of macrophages to resemble M2 phenotype (McWhorter et al., 2013) (Figure 5c) and increased expression of M2 markers: Cd206, Arg1 and Cc3cr1 (Figure 5c), but not M1 markers: iNos, Ccr2, Ifnar2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data.

claim: MYC/Twist1-HCC cells had increased secretion of cytokines: Il13, Ccl2, Ccl5, Ccl7 and Cxcl1 (p<0.05; Fold change ≥2, mean ≥20 ng/ml).
source: A multiplex ELISA for 38 cytokines was performed (Figure 5d) identifying that MYC/Twist1-HCC cells had increased secretion of cytokines: Il13, Ccl2, Ccl5, Ccl7 and Cxcl1 (p<0.05; Fold change ≥2, mean ≥20 ng/ml) (Figure 5e, Figure 5—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by multiplex ELISA data.

claim: Il13, Ccl2, Ccl5, Ccl7 and Cxcl1 were confirmed to be transcriptionally upregulated in MYC/Twist1- vs. MYC cells by qPCR.
source: These five cytokines were confirmed to be transcriptionally upregulated in MYC/Twist1- vs. to MYC cells by qPCR (Figure 5e).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data.

claim: Antibodies that neutralize Ccl2, Ccl5, Ccl7 or Cxcl1 inhibited the ability of conditioned media from MYC/Twist1-HCC to promote migration of macrophages.
source: Antibodies that neutralize Ccl2, Ccl5, Ccl7 or Cxcl1 inhibited the ability of conditioned media from MYC/Twist1-HCC to promote migration of macrophages (Figure 5f–h).
evidence: This is supported by transwell migration assay data with neutralizing antibodies.

claim: Neutralization of Ccl2 decreased macrophage migration 7-fold (p<0.0001).
source: Neutralization of Ccl2 decreased migration 7-fold (p<0.0001), Ccl5 1.2-fold (p=0.001), Ccl7 1.8-fold (p=0.001) and Cxcl1 2.1-fold (p=0.0002).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data from migration assays.

claim: Neutralization of Ccl5 decreased macrophage migration 1.2-fold (p=0.001).
source: Neutralization of Ccl2 decreased migration 7-fold (p<0.0001), Ccl5 1.2-fold (p=0.001), Ccl7 1.8-fold (p=0.001) and Cxcl1 2.1-fold (p=0.0002).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data from migration assays.

claim: Neutralization of Ccl7 decreased macrophage migration 1.8-fold (p=0.001).
source: Neutralization of Ccl2 decreased migration 7-fold (p<0.0001), Ccl5 1.2-fold (p=0.001), Ccl7 1.8-fold (p=0.001) and Cxcl1 2.1-fold (p=0.0002).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data from migration assays.

claim: Neutralization of Cxcl1 decreased macrophage migration 2.1-fold (p=0.0002).
source: Neutralization of Ccl2 decreased migration 7-fold (p<0.0001), Ccl5 1.2-fold (p=0.001), Ccl7 1.8-fold (p=0.001) and Cxcl1 2.1-fold (p=0.0002).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data from migration assays.

claim: Neutralizing Il13 did not affect macrophage migration (p=ns, FC 1.2).
source: Neutralizing Il13 (p=ns, FC 1.2) did not affect macrophage migration.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data from migration assays.

claim: Neutralization of Ccl2 inhibited the recruitment of macrophages into MYC/Twist1-spheroids by 3D culture.
source: Also, we found that the neutralization of Ccl2 inhibited the recruitment of macrophages into MYC/Twist1-spheroids by 3D culture (Figure 5—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is supported by 3D spheroid co-culture assay data.

claim: Neutralization of Il13 blocked M2 polarization by 50-fold reduction in Cd206 expression (p<0.0001) and 7-fold decrease in Arg1 (p<0.0001) without any change in M1 markers.
source: We found that neutralization of Il13 blocked M2 polarization by 50-fold reduction in Cd206 expression (p<0.0001) and 7-fold decrease in Arg1 (p<0.0001) without any change in M1 markers.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data from macrophage polarization assays.

claim: Neutralization of Ccl5 led to a 4-fold reduction in Cd206 (p<0.001) and 1.1-fold decrease in Arg1 (p<0.05).
source: Neutralization of Ccl5 led to a 4-fold reduction in Cd206 (p<0.001) and 1.1-fold decrease in Arg1 (p<0.05) and Cxcl1 led to 2.4-fold decrease in Cd206 (p<0.001) without significant change in Arg1 (p=ns) (Figure 5i).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data from macrophage polarization assays.

claim: Neutralization of Cxcl1 led to 2.4-fold decrease in Cd206 (p<0.001) without significant change in Arg1 (p=ns).
source: Neutralization of Ccl5 led to a 4-fold reduction in Cd206 (p<0.001) and 1.1-fold decrease in Arg1 (p<0.05) and Cxcl1 led to 2.4-fold decrease in Cd206 (p<0.001) without significant change in Arg1 (p=ns) (Figure 5i).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data from macrophage polarization assays.

claim: Adding Il13, but not Ccl2, to co-cultured MYC-HCC cells increased M2 markers expression.
source: Conversely, adding the cytokines Il13, but not Ccl2, to co-cultured MYC-HCC cells increased M2 markers expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data from co-culture experiments.

claim: MYC and TWIST1 promoter binding was identified upstream of human CCL2 and IL13 protein-coding genes in Gene Transcription Regulation Database (GTRD).
source: We identified MYC and TWIST1 promoter binding upstream of human CCL2 and IL13 protein-coding genes in Gene Transcription Regulation Database (GTRD), a meta-analysis of Chip-seq experiments (Dreos et al. 2017; Yevshin et al., 2019) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of ChIP-seq data from public databases, with citations.

claim: Both MYC and Twist1 demonstrated binding at multiple sites in the promoter regions of CCL2 and IL13 in the ChIP-seq data from several different cancer cell lines.
source: Both MYC and Twist1 demonstrated binding at multiple sites in the promoter regions of CCL2 and IL13 in the ChIP-seq data from several different cancer cell lines (Figure 5—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of ChIP-seq data.

claim: Multiple potential MYC and Twist1 transcription factor binding sites were found for both mouse Ccl2 and Il13 using motif finding analysis.
source: Again, we found multiple potential MYC and Twist1 transcription factor binding sites for both Ccl2 and Il13 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1f).
evidence: This is supported by motif finding analysis of promoter databases.

claim: MYC and Twist1 cooperate to transcriptionally regulate expression of Ccl2 and Il13 in the cancer cells.
source: These data suggest that MYC and Twist1 cooperate to transcriptionally regulate expression of Ccl2 and Il13 in the cancer cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq and motif analysis data.

claim: Control mice with orthotopic MYC-HCC did not develop metastatic nodules even though scattered, single cells were found in the lungs.
source: Control mice did not develop metastatic nodules even though scattered, single cells were found in the lungs (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis.

claim: No mice treated with Ccl2 alone (p=0.390, FC = 3) or Il13 alone (p=0.99, FC = 1) exhibited intrahepatic or pulmonary metastases.
source: No mice treated with Ccl2 alone (p=0.390, FC = 3) or Il13 alone (p=0.99, FC = 1) exhibited intrahepatic or pulmonary metastases (Figure 6c, e and g).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: All orthotopic MYC-HCC mice treated with the combination of Ccl2 and Il13 developed intrahepatic metastases (p=0.008, FC 2.5) and multifocal pulmonary metastases (p=0.02, FC = 104.4).
source: All orthotopic MYC-HCC mice treated with the combination of Ccl2 and Il13 developed intrahepatic metastases (p=0.008, FC 2.5) and multifocal pulmonary metastases (p=0.02, FC = 104.4) (Figure 6c, e and g).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: Both Ccl2 and Il13 are sufficient to elicit MYC-HCC to metastasize, even if Twist1 is not expressed in the tumor cells.
source: Hence, both Ccl2 and Il13 are sufficient to elicit MYC-HCC to metastasize, even if Twist1 is not expressed in the tumor cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cytokine treatment experiments.

claim: The combined treatment with Ccl2 and Il13 increased macrophage infiltration at both the orthotopic primary tumor in the liver and pulmonary metastases (p<0.0001).
source: The combined treatment with Ccl2 and Il13 increased macrophage infiltration at both the orthotopic primary tumor in the liver and pulmonary metastases (p<0.0001) (Figure 6e and h), with enrichment of M2-like Cd206+ TAMs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a-b).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data.

claim: Combined treatment with Ccl2 and Il13 resulted in enrichment of M2-like Cd206+ TAMs.
source: The combined treatment with Ccl2 and Il13 increased macrophage infiltration at both the orthotopic primary tumor in the liver and pulmonary metastases (p<0.0001) (Figure 6e and h), with enrichment of M2-like Cd206+ TAMs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a-b).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data.

claim: Treatment with Ccl2 alone increased macrophage recruitment 1.8-fold (p=0.001) but did not induce metastasis.
source: Treatment with Ccl2 alone increased macrophage recruitment 1.8-fold (p=0.001) but did not induce metastasis (Figure 6c, d, f and g).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: Treatment with Il13 alone did not increase either macrophage infiltration or induce metastasis.
source: On the other hand, treatment with Il13 alone did not increase either macrophage infiltration or induce metastasis (Figure 6e and h).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: In vivo treatment of MYC-HCC with combination of Ccl2 and Il13 stimulated angiogenesis.
source: Also, in vivo treatment of MYC-HCC with combination of Ccl2 and Il13 stimulated angiogenesis. The most significant increase in angiogenesis, as assessed by Cd31 IHC staining, was noted in MYC-HCC tumors in mice treated with Ccl2 and Il13 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data for CD31.

claim: Treatment with recombinant Il4 did not elicit either macrophage recruitment or increase metastasis.
source: As a negative control, treatment with recombinant Il4, a cytokine which was not increased in MYC/Twist1-HCC was performed. Il4 did not elicit either macrophage recruitment or increase metastasis (Figure 6—figure supplement 1d-e).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data with Il4 as a negative control.

claim: Combination of Ccl2 and Il13 induces metastasis of MYC-HCC associated with macrophage recruitment and polarization.
source: Thus, combination of Ccl2 and Il13 induces metastasis of MYC-HCC associated with macrophage recruitment and polarization.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cytokine treatment experiments.

claim: There was no statistical difference in orthotopic primary liver tumor burden between the four antibody treatment groups.
source: We first confirmed that there was no statistical difference in orthotopic primary liver tumor burden between the four groups by quantifying primary tumor volume. Quantification of BLI imaging showed a trend towards decrease but no statistical difference in liver tumor burden between the four groups (Figure 7b–c).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative imaging data.

claim: Control antibody treated mice developed multifocal intrahepatic and pulmonary metastases with extensive macrophage infiltration.
source: Control antibody treated mice, as expected, developed multifocal intrahepatic and pulmonary metastases with extensive macrophage infiltration (Figure 7c–e).
evidence: This is supported by histological and immunohistochemistry data.

claim: Inhibition of Ccl2 alone led to 7-fold decrease (p=0.002) in lung metastasis.
source: Inhibition of Ccl2 alone led to 7-fold decrease (p=0.002) and Il13 alone to a 2.5-fold decrease (p=0.03) in lung metastasis (Figure 7c and e).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data from antibody treatment experiments.

claim: Inhibition of Il13 alone led to a 2.5-fold decrease (p=0.03) in lung metastasis.
source: Inhibition of Ccl2 alone led to 7-fold decrease (p=0.002) and Il13 alone to a 2.5-fold decrease (p=0.03) in lung metastasis (Figure 7c and e).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data from antibody treatment experiments.

claim: Treatment with combination of anti-Ccl2 and anti-Il13 antibodies showed synergism, and led to a 12-fold decrease in liver metastases (p=0.0006) and 14-fold decrease in lung metastases (p=0.0009).
source: Further, treatment with combination of anti-Ccl2 and anti-Il13 antibodies showed synergism, and led to a 12-fold decrease in liver metastases (p=0.0006, Figure 7c and d) and 14-fold decrease in lung metastases (p=0.0009) (Figure 7c and e).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data from antibody treatment experiments.

claim: The combined inhibition of Ccl2 and Il13 led to dramatic reduction in macrophage recruitment (p<0.0001, FC 7.1).
source: The combined inhibition of Ccl2 and Il13 was noted to lead to dramatic reduction in macrophage recruitment (p<0.0001, FC 7.1)(Figure 7c and f) and polarization to M2-like phenotype (Figure 7—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data.

claim: The combined inhibition of Ccl2 and Il13 led to reduction in polarization to M2-like phenotype.
source: The combined inhibition of Ccl2 and Il13 was noted to lead to dramatic reduction in macrophage recruitment (p<0.0001, FC 7.1)(Figure 7c and f) and polarization to M2-like phenotype (Figure 7—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data.

claim: The inhibition of Ccl2 alone (p<0.001, FC 4.0), but not Il13 (p=0.435), decreased macrophage recruitment.
source: The inhibition of Ccl2 alone (p<0.001, FC 4.0), but not Il13 (p=0.435), decreased macrophage recruitment (Figure 7c and f).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data.

claim: Inhibition of Il13, either alone or in combination with Ccl2, led to loss of M2-like Cd206+ or Arg1+ macrophages in primary or metastatic sites.
source: While inhibition of Il13, either alone or in combination with Ccl2, led to loss of M2-like Cd206+ or Arg1+ macrophages in primary or metastatic sites (Figure 7—figure supplement 1a–b).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data.

claim: Inhibition of Ccl2 and Il13 decrease macrophage recruitment and polarization respectively.
source: Thus, inhibition of Ccl2 and Il13 decrease macrophage recruitment and polarization respectively.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the antibody treatment experiments.

claim: Treatment with anti-Il4 antibody had no effect on metastasis or macrophage recruitment in MYC/Twist1-HCC bearing mice.
source: As a control, mice bearing MYC/Twist1-HCC were treated with anti-Il4 antibody, which we show had no effect on metastasis or macrophage recruitment (Figure 7—figure supplement 1 c–e).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data with Il4 antibody as a negative control.

claim: Combined inhibition of Ccl2 and Il13 synergistically reduced macrophage recruitment and polarization thus blocking metastases.
source: Therefore, combined inhibition of Ccl2 and Il13 synergistically reduced macrophage recruitment and polarization thus blocking metastases (Figure 7g).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the antibody treatment experiments.

claim: Increased MYC and TWIST1 expression was associated with significantly worse disease-free survival (DFS) (p=4.3×10−10) in the pan-cancer cohort.
source: Increased MYC and TWIST1 expression was associated with significantly worse disease-free survival (DFS) (p=4.3×10−10) in the pan-cancer cohort (Figure 8a).
evidence: This is supported by survival analysis of TCGA data.

claim: Combined overexpression of MYC, TWIST1, CCL2 and IL13 predicted a slightly worse disease-free survival than MYC+TWIST1 overexpression alone (p=2.9×10−12).
source: Combined overexpression of MYC, TWIST1, CCL2 and IL13 predicted a slightly worse disease-free survival than MYC+TWIST1 overexpression alone (p=2.9×10−12) (Figure 8a).
evidence: This is supported by survival analysis of TCGA data.

claim: In a cohort of 144 patients with metastatic HCC, combined overexpression of MYC and TWIST1 was associated with significantly worse prognosis than either MYC or TWIST1 alone.
source: In another cohort of 144 patients with metastatic HCC, combined overexpression of MYC and TWIST1 was associated with significantly worse prognosis than either MYC or TWIST1 alone (Figure 8b).
evidence: This is supported by survival analysis of the GSE364 dataset.

claim: Compared to MYC/TWIST1Low tumors, MYC/TWIST1High tumors were infiltrated with significantly higher proportion of monocytes (2.9% vs 4.4%; p<0.001) and M2 macrophages (22% vs 26%, p<0.001).
source: Compared to MYC/TWIST1Low tumors, MYC/TWIST1High tumors were infiltrated with significantly higher proportion of monocytes (2.9% vs 4.4%; p<0.001) and M2 macrophages (22% vs 26%, p<0.001), while there was a lower proportion of M0 (10% vs 7%, p<0.001) and M1 macrophages (6% vs 4%, p<0.001) (Figure 8c).
evidence: This is supported by CIBERSORT analysis of TCGA data.

claim: MYC/TWIST1High tumors had a lower proportion of M0 (10% vs 7%, p<0.001) and M1 macrophages (6% vs 4%, p<0.001) compared to MYC/TWIST1Low tumors.
source: Compared to MYC/TWIST1Low tumors, MYC/TWIST1High tumors were infiltrated with significantly higher proportion of monocytes (2.9% vs 4.4%; p<0.001) and M2 macrophages (22% vs 26%, p<0.001), while there was a lower proportion of M0 (10% vs 7%, p<0.001) and M1 macrophages (6% vs 4%, p<0.001) (Figure 8c).
evidence: This is supported by CIBERSORT analysis of TCGA data.

claim: In the HCC cohort, MYC/TWIST1High tumors had higher M2 macrophages (24% vs 28% p=0.001).
source: This was also true in the HCC cohort (M2 macrophages 24% vs 28% p=0.001; Figure 8c).
evidence: This is supported by CIBERSORT analysis of HCC TCGA data.

claim: Combined MYC and TWIST1 expression strongly correlated with the expression of M2 macrophage related genes in the pan-cancer TCGA data.
source: Moreover, combined MYC and TWIST1 expression strongly correlated with the expression of M2 macrophage related genes in the pan-cancer TCGA data (Figure 8d).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis of TCGA data.

claim: Increased TAM infiltration in HCC was highly prognostic of overall survival on univariate and multivariate analysis (p=0.01, HR 16.0).
source: Increased TAM infiltration in HCC was highly prognostic of overall survival on univariate and multivariate analysis (p=0.01, HR 16.0, Figure 8—figure supplement 1c-e).
evidence: This is supported by survival analysis of HCC TCGA data.

claim: M2-like TAMs were associated with presence of vascular invasion, advanced stage and poor tumor grade in HCC.
source: Also, M2-like TAMs were associated with presence of vascular invasion, advanced stage and poor tumor grade (Figure 8—figure supplement 1f) in HCC.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis of HCC TCGA data.

claim: Combined MYC and TWIST1 expression correlated strongly with CCL2 and IL13 in the pan-cancer cohort (p=1.4×10−109).
source: Further, combined MYC and TWIST1 expression correlated strongly with CCL2 and IL13 in the pan-cancer cohort (p=1.4×10−109) (Figure 8d).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis of TCGA data.

claim: MYC and TWIST1 predict poor survival, CCL2/IL13 expression and M2-like TAM infiltration in human cancers.
source: Thus, MYC and TWIST1 predict poor survival, CCL2/IL13 expression and M2-like TAM infiltration in human cancers.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TCGA data analysis.

claim: Huh7 is a MYC/TWIST1Low cell line and SNU398 is a MYC/TWIST1High cell line.
source: We identified Huh7 as a MYC/TWIST1Low cell line and SNU398 as MYC/TWIST1High cell line (Figure 8e).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data from cell line screening.

claim: The MYC/TWIST1High cells transcriptionally expressed significantly higher levels of CCL2 and IL13 when compared to the MYC/TWIST1Low cells.
source: The MYC/TWIST1High cells transcriptionally expressed significantly higher levels of CCL2 and IL13 when compared to the MYC/TWIST1Low cells (Figure 8e).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data from cell lines.

claim: Conditioned media from MYC/TWIST1High cells polarized macrophages to M2-like phenotype while conditioned media from MYC/TWIST1Low cells induced a M1-like phenotype.
source: Conditioned media from MYC/TWIST1High cells polarized macrophages to M2-like phenotype while conditioned media from MYC/TWIST1Low cells induced a M1-like phenotype (Figure 8g).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data from macrophage polarization assays with human cell lines.

claim: Combined MYC and TWIST1 in human HCC cells lines is associated with CCL2 and IL13 secretion and macrophage M2-like polarization.
source: Thus, combined MYC and TWIST1 in human HCC cells lines is associated with CCL2 and IL13 secretion and macrophage M2-like polarization.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the human cell line experiments.

claim: Both CCL2 (p=0.006) and IL13 (p<0.0001), were significantly elevated in the plasma of patients with HCC but not cirrhosis.
source: Both CCL2 (p=0.006) and IL13 (p<0.0001), were significantly elevated in the plasma of patients with HCC but not cirrhosis (Figure 8h).
evidence: This is supported by clinical data from patient plasma samples.

claim: Increased expression of IL13, but not CCL2, was associated with the presence of multifocal tumors (p=0.04).
source: Increased expression of IL13, but not CCL2, was associated with the presence of multifocal tumors (p=0.04), suggestive of association with aggressive phenotype (Figure 8i).
evidence: This is supported by clinical correlation analysis.

claim: IL13 levels were higher in the plasma of patients with HCC with vascular invasion (p=0.01).
source: Also, IL13 levels were higher in the plasma of patients with HCC with vascular invasion, which is a known indicator of metastatic tumor spread in HCC (p=0.01) (Figure 8j).
evidence: This is supported by clinical correlation analysis.

claim: The plasma levels of the cytokines CCL2 and IL13 are elevated in patients with HCC, and higher IL13 levels predict multifocal and invasive HCC.
source: Thus, the plasma levels of the cytokines CCL2 and IL13 are elevated in patients with HCC, and higher IL13 levels predict multifocal and invasive HCC.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the clinical study data.

claim: MYC and TWIST1 drive metastasis by eliciting a transcriptional program in cancer cells that induces cytokines that in turn enable crosstalk between tumor and host, thus eliciting the recruitment and polarization of macrophages.
source: We found that MYC and TWIST1 drive metastasis by eliciting a transcriptional program in cancer cells that induces cytokines that in turn enable crosstalk between tumor and host, thus eliciting the recruitment and polarization of macrophages (Figure 9).
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from all the experimental data.

claim: This is the first autochthonous transgenic mouse model of HCC metastasis by hepatocyte-specific expression of MYC and Twist1.
source: To perform our studies, we have generated the first autochthonous transgenic mouse model of HCC metastasis by hepatocyte-specific expression of MYC and Twist1 that will be useful to study tumor progression and identify new therapies.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the model.

claim: Constitutive expression of both MYC and Twist1 is required for metastasis.
source: We demonstrate that constitutive expression of both MYC and Twist1 is required for metastasis.
evidence: This is supported by experiments showing that inactivation of either gene abrogates metastasis.

claim: MYC and Twist1 coordinate to regulate a cytokinome, including Ccl2 and Il13, that both are necessary and sufficient to elicit metastasis.
source: MYC and Twist1 coordinate to regulate a cytokinome, including Ccl2 and Il13, that both are necessary and sufficient to elicit metastasis.
evidence: This is supported by cytokine treatment and blockade experiments.

claim: In a prospective clinical analysis, human patients with HCC but not cirrhosis had increased plasma levels of CCL2 and IL13 that was associated with invasive and multifocal disease.
source: In a prospective clinical analysis, human patients with HCC but not cirrhosis had increased plasma levels of CCL2 and IL13 that was associated with invasive and multifocal disease.
evidence: This is supported by clinical data from patient plasma samples.

claim: MYC and TWIST1 are general drivers of metastasis.
source: We conclude that MYC and TWIST1 are general drivers of metastasis.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the mouse model, human cell line, and clinical data.

claim: The model enabled interrogation of tumor and host interactions during malignant progression in an immunocompetent host.
source: Our models enabled us to interrogate tumor and host interactions during malignant progression in an immunocompetent host.
evidence: This describes a feature of the mouse model.

claim: Through the Tet system, inducible combined MYC and Twist1 expression was elicited restricted to the hepatocytes.
source: Through the Tet system, we were able to elicit inducible combined MYC and Twist1 expression restricted to the hepatocytes.
evidence: This describes a feature of the mouse model.

claim: Greater than 90% of the mice predictably develop extrahepatic metastasis in the model.
source: In our model, greater than 90% of the mice predictably developing extrahepatic metastasis.
evidence: This is supported by observational data from the mouse model.

claim: This work is the first to suggest that MYC and Twist1 generally cooperate to drive metastasis.
source: Our work is the first to suggest that MYC and Twist1 generally cooperate to drive metastasis.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: MYC and Twist1 may contribute to metastasis through a transcriptional mechanism of inducing a cytokinome that activates macrophages.
source: Thus, our results suggest that MYC and Twist1 may contribute to metastasis through a transcriptional mechanism of inducing a cytokinome that activates macrophages.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the data.

claim: This work is the first to suggest that MYC and Twist1 together affect transcription in a manner that modulates innate immunity, thereby driving metastasis.
source: However, our work is the first to suggest that MYC and Twist1 together affect transcription in a manner that modulates innate immunity, thereby driving metastasis.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: Overexpression of MYC and TWIST1 in a tumor may be activating an embryonic program of innate immune cell activation and cellular invasion.
source: We propose as a possible general explanation for our findings that overexpression of MYC and TWIST1 in a tumor is activating an embryonic program of innate immune cell activation and cellular invasion.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: MYC and TWIST1 have been reported to cooperate during embryogenesis.
source: MYC and TWIST1 have been reported to cooperate during embryogenesis (Bellmeyer et al., 2003; Rodrigues et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: MYC and TWIST1 have been shown to transcriptionally modulate inflammation during embryogenesis.
source: The two transcription factors also have been shown to transcriptionally modulate inflammation during embryogenesis (Hurlin, 2013; Rodrigues et al., 2008; Spicer et al., 1996).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Microenvironment changes are required to enable mesodermal cells to migrate to their destination during embryogenesis.
source: These microenvironment changes are required to enable mesodermal cells to migrate to their destination (Šošić et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Both MYC and TWIST1 are overexpressed in multiple human cancers.
source: Both MYC and TWIST1 are overexpressed in multiple human cancers, suggesting there is a common embryonic transcriptional program they regulate in the embryonic microenvironment which is hijacked by cancer cells (Hendrix et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: MYC and TWIST1 overexpression in cancer may be eliciting tumor invasion by activating embryonic programs that otherwise physiologically enable mesodermal migration.
source: Hence, MYC and TWIST1 overexpression in cancer may be eliciting tumor invasion by activating embryonic programs that otherwise physiologically enable mesodermal migration.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: Ccl2 induced macrophage recruitment alone was not sufficient to cause metastasis in vivo.
source: However, our study further demonstrates Ccl2 induced macrophage recruitment alone was not sufficient to cause metastasis in vivo and Il13 induced macrophage polarization plays an essential and complementary role in promoting angiogenesis and metastasis.
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: Il13 induced macrophage polarization plays an essential and complementary role in promoting angiogenesis and metastasis.
source: However, our study further demonstrates Ccl2 induced macrophage recruitment alone was not sufficient to cause metastasis in vivo and Il13 induced macrophage polarization plays an essential and complementary role in promoting angiogenesis and metastasis.
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: Ccl2 and Il13 alone can enable a non-metastatic cancer to become metastatic, cell non-autonomously.
source: Further, our results suggest that Ccl2 and Il13 alone can enable a non-metastatic cancer to become metastatic, cell non-autonomously.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cytokine treatment experiments.

claim: Metastasis can occur during circumstances that would promote inflammation such as surgery or during infection.
source: In this regard, it is notable that there are anecdotal reports suggesting that metastasis can occur during circumstances that would promote inflammation such as surgery (Tohme et al., 2017) or during infection (Smith and Kang, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Stratifying patients based on cytokine expression may help direct therapy.
source: Stratifying patients based on cytokine expression may help direct therapy.
evidence: This is a clinical implication inferred from the findings.

claim: Inhibition of CCL2 alone has not been effective in clinical trials for solid tumors.
source: Inhibition of CCL2 alone has not been effective in clinical trials for solid tumors (Brana et al., 2015; Lim et al., 2016; Pienta et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to clinical trials.

claim: Personalized therapy that combines the inhibition of CCL2 and IL13 is more likely to be effective.
source: We suggest that personalized therapy that combines the inhibition of CCL2 and IL13 is more likely to be effective.
evidence: This is a therapeutic implication inferred from the findings.

claim: Two transcription factors, MYC and TWIST1, are key drivers of metastasis.
source: Our work identifies two transcription factors, MYC and TWIST1, are key drivers of metastasis.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the work.

claim: MYC and TWIST1 elicit a cytokinome, that includes CCL2 and IL13, enabling crosstalk between cancer cells and host macrophages that drives tumor progression.
source: Together, they elicit a cytokinome, that includes CCL2 and IL13, enabling crosstalk between cancer cells and host macrophages that drives tumor progression.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the work.
